chapter.title: Programs Written for CLR.CLS
chapter.para: BSF4ooRexx's CLR.CLS (by Rony G. Flatscher, with Manuel Raffel and Adrian Baginski) reached .NET Framework through Java and jni4net. The bridge has a CLR.CLS of its own, a thin compatibility package over net.cls, so that programs written for that one run unchanged, on .NET 8 or later, without Java: a program that says ::REQUIRES CLR.CLS finds it next to net.cls. Everything the package does not mention is net.cls's: events, properties, enums, arrays, conversions.

example.title: A program written for CLR.CLS
example.programlisting:
console = clr.import("System.Console") console~WriteLine("Hello from CLR.CLS") sb = .clr~new("System.Text.StringBuilder", "ab") say sb~Append("c")~ToString pp(sb~Length) say .clr~new("System.DateTime")~Now~Year > 2000
::requires CLR.CLS

table.title: CLR.CLS's interface, as this package gives it

a CLR (a subclass of NetObject) for a new object of that type; a wrapper type ("System.Int16" ... "System.String") with one value: that value boxed, as clr.box

the same, put in .local by default under the type's name, as CLR.CLS
the .NET member of that name, whatever Rexx method shares it
o~clr.object, o~clr.type
the proxy itself (there is no Java peer); its System.Type

a .NET array, a NetArray, from 1

a proxy: a .NET object as itself, a Rexx number boxed as Int32, Int64 or Decimal, any other string as a System.String

section.title: What the Package Adds to net.cls
section.para: For the objects it makes, and every .NET object they return (which stay proxies of its own, isA(.CLR)):

listitem.para: A whole number argument goes as an Int32 (an Int64 past its range), as clr.wrap made it: programs written for CLR.CLS rely on it (Convert~ToChar(stream~Read) must choose ToChar(int)). So a Rexx string that looks like a whole number no longer reaches a string parameter (sb~Append("007") appends 7), as in CLR.CLS. A property's value converts to the property's type.
The static Process.Start(file [, arguments]) goes through the shell, as on .NET Framework: a document or a URL opens with its application.
Instance and static members together, as CLR.CLS found them: .clr~new("System.DateTime")~Now.
An imported type also reaches its System.Type's members, when no static member has the name: clr.import("System.String")~Name.

section.para: What stays different. say o shows a CLR_PROXY (System.Text.StringBuilder #12) (o~ToString gives the text); clr.object and clr.type are .NET objects of this bridge, not BSF4ooRexx's Java peers; types are found as net.cls finds them, not through Assembly.LoadWithPartialName. MainMenu and System.Device.Location do not exist in .NET 8.

When the binary release is installed and BSF4ooRexx's own CLR.CLS is found on the REXX_PATH or the PATH, the installer does not put this one beside rexx (rexx install --clr does), so that the programs written for that one keep it; a program finds a CLR.CLS in its own directory before any other.
